info.title: AgentEval.Cli
info.description: AgentEval CLI — terminal + CI/CD entry point for the .NET evaluation toolkit. The agenteval init command bootstraps a .agenteval/ workspace; agenteval bench {gdpr|eu-ai-act|agentic|owasp|mitre|perf|longmemeval|memory} runs benchmark families; agenteval mc serve launches the local Mission Control portal (requires .NET 10); agenteval doctor verifies workspace integrity via canonical-JSON audit-chain hashing.

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription: AgentEval CLI — evaluate AI agents, run benchmark suites, manage the .agenteval/ output store, and serve Mission Control.

options.name: --i-understand-live-side-effects
options.description: Required consent for --sut copilot-studio: acknowledge that scanning a LIVE agent can fire real connector/flow actions. Use a NON-PROD agent. Without this the command refuses before any network call. [default: False]

options.name: --max-credits
options.description: Cap the Copilot Credits a live --sut copilot-studio run may spend (0 = no cap). ENFORCED as an ESTIMATE — the SDK exposes no real credit-cost field, so this counts turns (1 estimated credit each), not actual metered spend, and a turn that would push spend past the cap never fires. The run then stops (redteam: exit 8/BudgetExceeded; eval/bench: their normal failure exit code). A real reasoning turn likely costs substantially MORE than this estimate counts — set the cap conservatively, and don't assume hitting it means the estimate overcounted. [default: 0]

options.name: --copilotstudio-save-config-baseline
options.description: After the Copilot Studio config resolves, write a trust-time agent-identity fingerprint pin (JSON) to this path. Opt-in; always overwrites (mirrors --save-baseline's convention).

options.name: --copilotstudio-config-baseline
options.description: Compare the resolved Copilot Studio config's agent-identity fingerprint against this pinned baseline file (from --copilotstudio-save-config-baseline). Drift WARNS by default (a stale/wrong-agent --baseline RESULT comparison would be meaningless); pass --fail-on-config-drift to hard-stop instead.

options.name: --fail-on-config-drift
options.description: With --copilotstudio-config-baseline: treat a detected agent-identity drift as a hard stop (refuse before any network call) instead of a warning. [default: False]

options.name: --system-prompt-canary
options.description: Secret token embedded in the SUT system prompt; SystemPromptExtraction then proves a leak only when this exact token appears in a response (otherwise Inconclusive).

options.name: --attacks
options.description: Comma-separated attack types (e.g., PromptInjection,Jailbreak). Default: all. Opt-in multi-turn: Crescendo, PAIR, TAP (PAIR/TAP require --attacker), ToolEscalation (best at --sut-tier instrumented).

options.name: --import-probes
options.description: Import a JSON or CSV seed-prompt dataset (HarmBench/JailbreakBench/etc.; dispatched by .json/.csv extension) and run it alongside the built-in attacks. Probes without an expected-token oracle are Inconclusive unless --judge is set.

options.name: --import-prompt-field
options.description: Column/field holding the prompt in --import-probes (default: 'Behavior' for .csv, 'prompt' for .json).

options.name: --import-id-column
options.description: Optional id column/field for --import-probes (falls back to row/array index).

options.name: --package-registry
options.description: SupplyChain (LLM03) package check: none (planted-fake proxy, default) | live (query PyPI/npm/NuGet to also flag model-invented hallucinated packages). [default: none]

options.name: --pack
options.description: Download + run an external benchmark pack: a catalog name (HarmBench, JailbreakBench, CyberSecEval), a data URL (.json/.csv), or 'list' to show the catalog. Named packs require --accept-license (no data is bundled).

options.name: --accept-license
options.description: Accept the upstream license of a --pack before downloading it (these datasets contain harmful content by design). [default: False]

options.name: --intensity
options.description: Scan intensity: quick | moderate | comprehensive [default: moderate]

options.name: --fail-fast
options.description: Stop scanning on first successful attack [default: False]

options.name: --max-probes
options.description: Maximum probes per attack (0 = unlimited) [default: 0]

options.name: --delay
options.description: Seconds to wait between probes (0 = none); throttle for a rate-limited gateway. [default: 0]

options.name: --parallelism
options.description: Concurrent probes WITHIN an attack (default 1). >1 requires a thread-safe agent — see ScanOptions.Parallelism. [default: 1]

options.name: --timeout-per-probe
options.description: Per-probe timeout in seconds (default 30; must be > 0 and <= 86400). [default: 30]

options.name: --max-turn-timeout
options.description: Per-turn timeout (seconds) for multi-turn attacks (0 = inherit --timeout-per-probe). [default: 0]

options.name: --judge
options.description: Separate endpoint for LLM judge (evaluates attack success)

options.name: --judge-model
options.description: Model for judge (default: same as --model)

options.name: --judge-mode
options.description: How the judge grades: 'primary' (default — ADR-023 B.3 flip; the Composite Judges grade semantic/text-only probes first, keyword oracle advisory) or 'fallback' (legacy — judge only adjudicates Inconclusive verdicts). 'primary' requires --judge; without it, a run is byte-identical to the keyword oracle. [default: primary]

options.name: --judge-rubric
options.description: Judge rubric for --judge-mode primary: 'evidence-anchored' (default — a conclusive verdict must be grounded in a verbatim quote from the response, which targets BOTH false alarms and missed hits, carries the per-oracle discriminators, and is the rubric the published κ/fabrication numbers were measured under), 'strict' (precision-oriented — only clear compromise ⇒ Succeeded; fewer false alarms but more missed hits; no discriminators), or 'lenient' (recall-oriented — any sign of compromise ⇒ Succeeded; catches more real compromises at the cost of more false alarms). For a scan where a missed vulnerability matters more than a false alarm, prefer 'lenient'. [default: evidence-anchored]

options.name: --judge-timeout
options.description: Grading timeout (seconds): bounds the single-judge/fallback path per judge call (keeps the advisory keyword verdict on timeout) AND the default judge-primary composite path as a total grading bound (abstains → Inconclusive on timeout). 0 = no separate bound; grading shares the per-probe budget (--timeout-per-probe). [default: 0]

options.name: --judge-api-key
options.description: API key for the judge endpoint (--judge). Falls back to --api-key if omitted.

options.name: --attacker
options.description: Endpoint for the attacker LLM (drives Crescendo/PAIR/TAP; non-deterministic). Required by PAIR/TAP.

options.name: --attacker-model
options.description: Model for the attacker LLM (default: same as --model)

options.name: --attacker-api-key
options.description: API key for the attacker endpoint (--attacker). Falls back to --api-key if omitted.

options.name: --format
options.description: Export format: json | sarif | markdown | md | junit | nist (NIST AI RMF JSON) | nist-md (NIST AI RMF Markdown) [default: markdown]

options.name: -o
options.description: Output file (default: stdout)

options.name: --save-baseline
options.description: After the scan, write a regression baseline (JSON) to this path.

options.name: --baseline-version
options.description: Version identifier stamped into the saved baseline (e.g. a release tag or commit SHA). Default: "unspecified".

options.name: --baseline-note
options.description: Free-text note stored in the saved baseline (--save-baseline).

options.name: --baseline
options.description: Compare the scan to this baseline (JSON), print the diff, and gate the exit code on regression.

options.name: --fail-on
options.description: Exit-code gate: vuln (any vulnerability) | regression (new vs --baseline) | never. [default: vuln]

options.name: --calibration
options.description: Calibrate the scan against a reference cohort (JSON: per-attack mean/stddev). Prints a z-score per attack — flags ones unusually vulnerable (≤−2σ) vs the cohort. The cohort is yours (no built-in).

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Show detailed progress [default: False]

options.name: --explain
options.description: Attach an LLM rationale to each Succeeded/Inconclusive finding, narrating the verdict + evidence fidelity. Requires --judge (no-op + warning otherwise); adds one judge call per explained finding. [default: False]

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Suppress all output except the export [default: False]

options.description:

Default: standard. Domain-pack composition: standard+healthcare | standard+hr | standard+childrens (multi-pack composition like standard+healthcare+hr also supported).

commands.name: agentic
commands.description: Run the agentic behavior benchmark

options.name: --preset
options.description:
Preset (sourced from BenchmarkFamilyRegistry):
agentic-execution — 6-evaluator system-outcome + agentic-process composite (canonical default)
tool-call-accuracy — Focused tool-call diagnostic (5 sub-dimensions)
rag-quality — RAG dimensions: groundedness, relevance, coherence, fluency, similarity, completeness, F1
judge-quality — Meta-evaluator: inter-rater agreement, calibration, drift
safety — 12-evaluator safety/security composite (requires policy resolver — programmatic only)
telemetry — 6 pure-code operational evaluators (latency, tokens, cost, errors, retries)
glass-box-diagnostics — 8 Glass Box trace evaluators, 7 pure-code (tool reliability/errors, safety interventions, truncation, prompt drift/injection, arg leaks, token skew) — requires --trace
stochastic-stability — Run-to-run score consistency (requires N prior run results)
conversational — 5-evaluator multi-turn quality composite
reasoning — 4-evaluator reasoning correctness composite
user-experience — 5-evaluator UX composite (tone, verbosity, refusal, confidence)
adversarial-direct — 3-evaluator adversarial-resistance composite (high-severity threshold)
Default: agentic-execution. judge-quality / telemetry / stochastic-stability are pure-code (no LLM cost); safety needs a programmatic policy resolver.

options.name: --budget-tier
options.description: Budget tier filter: trivial | low | medium | high | all (default: all). Components with a cost tier above the budget are filtered out and remaining weights are renormalized. Use 'low' or 'medium' for fast feedback loops; 'all' for full audit runs.

options.name: --trace
options.description: Path to a captured Glass Box trace (JSON). Attaches the dual-boundary trace to the evaluation so trace-aware evaluators (e.g. the glass-box-diagnostics preset) read real chat/tool-boundary data instead of skipping.

A skill whose content changed since the pin was captured is reported as a High-severity ManifestChangedSinceBaseline finding — gated by --fail-on-noncompliant like any other High finding, no separate flag needed. A possible rug-pull: a previously-approved skill silently changing after approval.
